body.p: REMARKS/ARGUMENTS
Upon entry of the present amendment, claims 2, 8-10, 12-18 will be pending in this

application. Claims 2 and 14 have been amended and claims 3-7 and 11 have been canceled. No new matter is added. Based on the following remarks, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and allowance of the pending claims.

Claim 6 is rejected under 35 USC § 112(b) or 35 USC § 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph, as allegedly indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor of a joint inventor (or for applications subject to pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, the applicant), regards as the invention. Office Action Page 2. Applicant has canceled this claim to render this rejection now moot.

Claims 2, 4, and 8-13 are rejected under 35 USC § 103(a) as allegedly unpatentable over US 2003/0228344 in the name of Fields et al. (hereinafter "Fields"), in view of US 2007/0043350 in the name of Soltesz (hereinafter "Soltesz"). Office Action pages 2-6. Claims 3, 7, and 14-18 are rejected under 35 USC § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over Fields in view of Soltesz as applied to claim 2 above, and further in view of US 2012/0149978 in the name of Oliveria et al. (hereinafter "Oliveria"). Office Action pages 6-7. Claims 5 and 6 are rejected under 35 USC § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over Fields in view of Soltesz as applied to claim
4 above, and further in view of US 2003/0036755 in the name of Ginn (hereinafter "Ginn"). Office Action pages 7-8.

In the sole interest of compact prosecution, Applicant has amended independent claim 1 to include the features of dependent claim 3 and further define the video-assisted thoracoscopic surgical device as follows:
A system for occluding a collateral flow channel and treating emphysema, the system comprising:

a video-assisted thoracoscopic surgical device that is configured to be inserted into a thoracic cavity of a patient to identify a collateral flow channel between a target lung compartment and an adjacent lung compartment;
a closure device that is configured to be inserted into the thoracic cavity of the patient

to close the collateral flow channel between the target lung compartment and the adjacent lung compartment and thereby disrupt the collateral flow channel, wherein the thoracic closure device comprises a stapling device; and
an endobronchial valve that is implantable in an airway leading to the target lung compartment to treat emphysema.

These features are not disclosed or suggested in the cited art references. As the Examiner appears to appreciate, "Fields fails to disclose a video-assisted thoracoscopic surgical device that is configured to be inserted into a thoracic cavity of a patient." Office Action, page 4. To cure this deficiency, the Examiner relies on Soltesz which is primarily directed to selective lung tissue ablation for effecting lung volume reduction. A brief mention in paragraph [0038] merely states that the One Lung Ventilation (OLV) technique can be combined with Video Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery (VATS). Soltesz does NOT however teach or suggest a VATS configured to identify a collateral flow channel between the target lung compartment and the adjacent lung compartment as presently claimed. Further, Soltesz does NOT teach or suggest a thoracic closure device comprising a stapling device that is configured to be inserted into the thoracic cavity of the patient to close the collateral flow channel from the thoracic cavity.

Regarding Olivera, the Examiner appears to appreciate that "neither Fields nor Soltesz discloses wherein the closure device comprises a stapling device." Office Action, page 6. The Examiner attempts to cure this deficiency with Olivera which is primarily direct to devices and systems for measuring airway diameters. In particular, the Examiner refers to paragraph [0043] as disclosing the claimed thoracic stapling device. This paragraph notes that the endoscopic closing mechanism 330 may comprise a staple. As shown in Fig. 4A reproduced below, the airway closing mechanism is in fact delivered endoscopically via a bronchoscope 200 through the mouth or nose of a patient and into the airways AW. In contrast, the presently claimed

stapler closure device is inserted into the thoracic cavity of the patient (i.e., through the chest wall via a surgical approach) facilitated by the video-assisted thoracoscopic surgical device which identifies the collateral flow channel to be disrupted.

In view of the foregoing, Applicant believes all claims now pending in this application are in condition for allowance. The issuance of a formal Notice of Allowance at an early date is respectfully requested.
